title: Payroll
protagonist: Francesca Molinari, founder and owner of Grampoline LLC
primary_metric: dollars removed from the $20,000 remaining-2019-payroll shortfall

options.A: Operation Clean Break -- let one employee go, closing the $20,000 shortfall in a single cut
options.B: Operation Shared Weight -- cut every remaining employee's pay by the same percentage, closing the same $20,000 shortfall

legacy_conversion_note: Original source (source/Y1/Session 2/Payroll/Case Study_ Payroll.docx, Guide Notes.docx, and Grampoline Annual Financial Report.xlsx) is a fictional small business (Grampoline LLC) invented by the original case materials -- unlike Cardiology (a real clinical trial) or LeBron Vs. Michael (real NBA statistics), there is no real-world entity to verify Grampoline's revenue, expenses, or payroll figures against. Every dollar figure in Appendix B and Appendix C is carried forward unchanged, digit for digit, from the original workbook's own 'Financial Data' sheet (Revenue/Expenses/Payroll/Profit by year, and each named employee's payroll by year including the 2019 'projected remaining' column) -- nothing was invented for this conversion; the figures are the case's own stated fictional dataset, disclosed as such rather than presented as sourced fact (see modeling_assumptions). The original Challenge's own two sub-questions ('If your position is A, who do you let go and why?' and 'If your position is B, whose pay do you cut and by how much?') are preserved unchanged as D3/D4, now with exact arithmetic forced against the real numbers in the source workbook: Tiago and Irene's H2-2019 projected pay are each exactly $20,000, so Option A closes the $20,000 target exactly only if one of those two is chosen; Option B's percent cut was computed against the $111,500 five-employee remaining-payroll pool (Francesca excluded -- she is not one of 'the five employees' the Dilemma names, and she has already gone without pay). Both options were deliberately kept mathematically identical on the primary metric (margin_pct = 0.0) because the source data makes them so by construction (Tiago/Irene's remaining pay coincidentally equals the shortfall exactly), which turns the case's real tension into a values question -- concentrated vs. distributed hardship -- rather than a financial-optimization question, matching the original 2020 Guide Notes' own framing ('What decision would provide the most financial value? What decision would be most helpful to others?'). The original Guide Notes' Anchor Question (a customer call revealing a personal connection to Irene) is formalized as this conversion's Twist with a disclosed, stated scenario assumption (the customer account = 15% of 2019 H1 revenue, MA3) rather than left as an unquantified narrative beat, so it forces a real recompute (D3-style) instead of only a discussion prompt.

modeling_assumptions.text: Grampoline LLC's financial history (Appendix B) and per-employee payroll (Appendix C) are the original case materials' own fictional dataset (Grampoline Annual Financial Report.xlsx), carried forward verbatim -- not a real company's real financial data, and therefore not subject to external verification. Profit = Revenue - Expenses - Payroll in every year of the source data, confirmed by recomputation.

The $20,000 shortfall and Option B's percent-cut base are both computed over the five named employees' H2-2019 projected pay ($111,500 total: Martha $22,500 + Paul $21,000 + Christina $28,000 + Tiago $20,000 + Irene $20,000). Francesca's own H2-2019 projected pay ($11,500) is excluded from both, since the Dilemma is specifically about 'employee' payroll and Francesca has already gone without pay this year.

Twist scenario assumption, disclosed and not a real sourced figure: the customer account credited to Irene's social media work in the Twist is assumed to represent 15% of Grampoline's 2019 H1 revenue ($127,000 x 15% = $19,050), at real risk of leaving within the following year if Irene's position ends. This figure exists only to give the Twist's narrative beat (present in the original 2020 Guide Notes as an unquantified Anchor Question) a real, computable consequence; it applies only to the branch where a Hero has chosen Operation Clean Break specifically via Irene.

deliverables.text: A bar graph comparing each of Grampoline's five employees' projected remaining 2019 pay.
A pie chart showing what percent share of the total remaining 2019 payroll each employee represents.
If Option A: the employee let go, the exact dollar amount removed from the remaining payroll budget, and how that compares to the $20,000 target in dollars and percent.
If Option B: the flat percent pay cut applied to all five employees that removes exactly $20,000, shown employee by employee with each person's new remaining-pay figure.
A comparison table weighing the chosen option against the other, using D1-D4's figures plus at least one non-financial factor from Appendix A.

balance.argument_a: Letting go of either Tiago or Irene removes exactly $20,000 from the remaining payroll budget in a single, clean cut -- the target is closed exactly, with zero risk of a second round of cuts from a rounding shortfall. The other four employees keep 100% of the pay they were counting on for the rest of the year, including Martha, who is already stretched thin caring for her niece and would face a second hardship on top of her first if her own pay were cut instead.
balance.argument_b: A 17.94% pay cut applied to all five employees closes the identical $20,000 gap without anyone losing their job, their income entirely, or their identity at the company. It spreads a real $20,000 hardship five ways instead of concentrating 100% of it onto one person and their household -- including Tiago, two months into fatherhood with a fiancee still recovering from a difficult pregnancy, and Irene, who just signed a year-long lease she can't easily break.
balance.margin_basis: Both options are constructed, by the source data itself, to close the identical $20,000 target: Tiago and Irene's H2-2019 projected pay (Appendix C) are each exactly $20,000 (Operation Clean Break), and 17.9372% of the five-employee $111,500 payroll pool is $20,000 exactly (Operation Shared Weight). margin_pct = 0.0 -- the two options genuinely do not differ on the graded primary metric. The case's real tension is who bears the $20,000 and how concentrated the impact is, not which option is financially better. See derived{} for the full worked figures.

derived._note: Computed during conversion from Appendix B/C's given data (itself carried forward verbatim from Grampoline Annual Financial Report.xlsx); case-readiness should re-derive independently, not just trust this block.

sensitivity_note: This case touches money stress and family hardship directly (Francesca going without pay, Martha's caregiving crisis, a real possibility of an employee losing their job) -- SPEC.md Sec.6 flags this for the discussion lead. See FACILITATOR.md's sensitivity note.
